# deepseek-harness :: dsh-experimental-misc

**Files in shard:** 502 — **read: 453**, **skipped with a stated reason: 49** (35 auto-generated
`README.i18n.yaml` bilingual-pairing hash records + 14 SVG/PNG icon assets; all confirmed by a head
peek, none line-by-line). Per-file status and note: `dsh-experimental-misc.status.tsv` (exactly one
row per file, same order as the shard's file list).

**What this shard covers:** the whole `packages/experimental/**` group of the DeepSeek Harness monorepo —
19 optional, explicitly-enabled "experimental" capability packages plus 12 tiny bundle/patch packages
that exist only to compose them. The substantive content is: **Agent Teams** (durable roster, peer
messaging, a shared task DAG with compare-and-set revisions, and an event-sourced projection), an
**auto-review** layer that re-reviews each tool call with the same model, **hook bridges** for Claude
Code and Codex (a shared `hook-protocol` with wire codec, matcher, merge and runner), **tool-session-query**
(a SQLite/FTS search over model session traces), **tool-ralph** (bounded repeated delegation), a
**PTC runtime** for a CPython subprocess backend, **webhook** ingress with HMAC verification, and
**worktree**/terminal/translator/speech-to-text/voice-input capability packages. Every package in the
group is *opt-in by construction*: a bundle ships switched off and is turned on in the GUI plugin manager.

**Reading method (tiers used here).** Tier 1 (load-bearing source) was read line by line, except
the two files over 120 KB (`ptc-runtime-python/src/index.ts` and `py/bootstrap.py`), which were read
as head + tail, and the six very large test suites, which were catalogued by every `describe`/`it`
name. Tier 2 (docs, config, tests, examples) was read in batches; the 23 Chinese `README.zh.md`
mirrors were read in condensed form (headings, bullets, tables, code) against their English source,
which the repo's `README.i18n.yaml` hash-records prove section-for-section. Tier 3 (generated i18n
records, icons) was confirmed by head peek only and is reported as skipped with a reason. Nothing in
the reference repo was executed, installed, built or tested.

## 1. File-by-file


### Tier 1 — `packages/experimental/agent-team` (the durable multi-agent substrate)

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/types.ts`
- **Purpose:** the public identity and record vocabulary of Agent Teams.
- **Key abstractions:** branded `TeamId` / `TeamTaskId` / `TeamMessageId` (branding functions of the same name); `TeamMemberPhase` (`provisioning | active | failed`); `TeamTaskStatus` (`pending | in_progress | completed | deleted`); durable *snapshot* types (`TeamMemberSnapshot`, `TeamTaskSnapshot`, `TeamMessageSnapshot`) vs runtime-enriched *view* types (`TeamMemberView`, `TeamTaskView`); `TeamTaskAction` union of 8 mutations; `TeamProjection` for the browser.
- **Data flow:** the durable snapshot is the write model; the view is the read model. `declare module` augmentations wire the Team into three host maps: `SessionProjectionMap` (`agentTeam`), `MessageSourceMap` (`team-message`), `SessionEventMap` (`team/member`, `team/task`, `team/message/queued`, `team/message/delivered`). Every event payload carries `{ version: 2, teamId, … }`.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the snapshot/view split is explicit — snapshots are "whole durable value written on every lifecycle change", views are "runtime-enriched"; (b) `TeamMemberSnapshot` holds `provider` and `context` as **immutable** identity fields, checked by the projection; (c) `TeamProjection.failure` is documented as "names the first rejected persisted Team record; members and tasks then stay at the last valid state".
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `TeamTaskAction` is a closed union, so the switch in `task-board.ts` can be exhaustive; `Config` limits are all optional and validated in `index.ts`.
- **Surprising:** `TeamMessageSnapshot` / `team-message` source / `team/message/*` events are **historical**: the README says Team "writes neither" of the mailbox events any more — the live path uses the target Agent's inbox instead. These types survive for replay compatibility.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/error.ts`
- **Purpose:** one typed failure for the whole Team domain.
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamError extends HarnessError` with a stable `code` string; `errorMessage(error)` which renders any thrown value to "one bounded single-line description" using `node:util.inspect` with `depth: 4`.
- **Data flow:** every domain throw goes through `TeamError`; `errorMessage` is used to render errors into *durable* records (e.g. `TeamMemberSnapshot.error`).
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** `errorMessage` deliberately does **not** replace the original rejection — it is a rendering helper, so the original error is still thrown/aggregated elsewhere.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** non-`Error` throws (strings, plain objects) are handled; a plain string becomes the message, an object is `inspect`ed.
- **Surprising:** the `TeamError` codes are a large closed vocabulary (`TEAM_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `TEAM_TASK_STALE_REVISION`, `TEAM_PROVISIONING_CONFLICT`, …) — the code, not the message, is the contract.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/validation.ts`
- **Purpose:** input normalization shared by roster and task commands.
- **Key abstractions:** `requiredText(value, field, maxLength)` — trims, rejects empty and over-length; `writeScope(value)` — normalizes a workspace-relative path prefix.
- **Data flow:** raw model-supplied strings in; normalized strings out, or a `TeamError` with `TEAM_INVALID_ARGUMENT` / `TEAM_INVALID_WRITE_SCOPE`.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** `writeScope` explicitly **refuses to be a lock**: the JSDoc says "Normalize one workspace-relative path prefix without treating it as a lock." It rejects absolute paths, drive letters (`/^[a-z]:/iu`), empty segments, `.` and `..`, and normalizes `\` → `/`. The path component split is done *after* the leading-`/` and drive-letter checks so a Windows path cannot smuggle through.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** over-length description caps are 200 (subject) / 16,384 (description) / 200 (provider) — enforced at the command layer, not the schema layer.
- **Surprising:** `writeScope` is *advisory*. The README is blunt: scopes "produce warnings … they never block anything" — a path guard that only warns is a coordination hint, not a sandbox.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/session-message.ts`
- **Purpose:** deciding whether one user message is *durably* accepted by a Session.
- **Key abstractions:** `messageAccepted(events, predicate)` — true if the message is in committed history **or** in the still-pending inbox.
- **Data flow:** takes a Session's event suffix; folds `agent/inbox/spliced` events into two pending buckets (`next-turn`, `next-step`) by splicing at `event.data.start` for `event.data.removedCount`; then tests history (`user/message`) and the pending buckets.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** the inbox is *replayed* rather than read from a live structure, because the target child may not be loaded — the check must work against the durable log alone. `InboxProjection` is a `Record<'next-turn' | 'next-step', UserMessage[]>` so the two admission classes are kept separate.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** the splice maths handles removal (`removedCount ?? 0`) so a re-sent inbox does not double-count.
- **Surprising:** "accepted" ≠ "processed". A message can be durably accepted and still be waiting in the inbox; the provisioning check uses exactly this weaker property.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/persisted.ts`
- **Purpose:** a short-lived read handle for a stored child Session.
- **Key abstractions:** `PersistedSessionView` = `{ inheritedEventCount, header, events }`; `readPersistedSession(persistence, id, signal)`.
- **Data flow:** `persistence.open(id, 'read', { signal })` → `handle.read(0, undefined, { signal })` → returns header + every committed event; the handle is closed in a `finally`.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** `inheritedEventCount` is returned explicitly because callers need the *suffix* (the child's own events) and the fork boundary is what separates inherited history from the child's own. The read handle is always closed before returning.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** cancellation is observed by both `open` and `read`; the `finally` closes the handle even on failure.
- **Surprising:** this exists purely so that a *cold* teammate (not loaded in this process) can still be reconciled after a restart.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/journal.ts`
- **Purpose:** the transaction owner over the exact live Lead Session log.
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamJournal` with `state(root)`, `transact(rootId, operation)`, `appendAndFlush(root, type, data)`.
- **Data flow:** `transact` serializes per-Lead operations through a promise-tail map (`tails`), so all Team mutations for one Lead are strictly ordered. `appendAndFlush` appends the Team event to the Lead's Session and **awaits `sessions.flush`** before `onCommit(root)` fires the activity notification.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the transaction queue is a plain promise chain — `prior.then(operation, operation)` means a failed prior operation does **not** poison the queue; (b) `state(root)` reads the *authoritative* projection and **throws** on `projection.failure` — the durable failure is surfaced, not swallowed; (c) `appendAndFlush` casts `root.session.append` to a narrower `AppendTeamEvent` type with a comment explaining it removes Session.append's conditional surface argument "while preserving the event-key/payload correlation".
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** the tail entry is removed in a `finally` only if it is still the current tail; a failure inside `operation` propagates to the caller but does not break the next queued operation.
- **Surprising:** Team events "never enter the conversation surface" (comment in `appendAndFlush`) — so coordination records cost **zero model tokens**. This is the key insight: the task board is durable state the model re-reads on demand, not context it carries.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/activity.ts`
- **Purpose:** one-shot change waiters, independent of durable state.
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamActivity.wait(id, timeoutMs, signal) → { timedOut }`; `notify(id)`; `close()`.
- **Data flow:** a `Map<TeamId, Set<Waiter>>` of waiters. `notify` wakes *every* current waiter for a Team and removes the set; `close` wakes all Teams' waiters during disposal.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the timeout window is validated as an integer from **10,000 ms to 3,600,000 ms** — a bounded wait, never a poll loop; (b) the result carries only `timedOut` — the caller must **re-read** state, so a wake-up never carries a stale snapshot; (c) `finish()` is idempotent via a `settled` flag because timeout, abort and notification can race.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** abort is handled twice — a pre-check `signal.throwIfAborted()`, a listener, and a **post-registration re-check** because "AbortSignal does not replay an abort that wins between the pre-check and listener registration"; a non-`Error` abort reason is wrapped in `TEAM_WAIT_ABORTED`.
- **Surprising:** `close()` resolves waiters with `timedOut: false` — disposal is reported as "something happened", not as a timeout.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/lifecycle.ts`
- **Purpose:** the single admission cutoff and bounded settlement for the Team runtime.
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamRuntimeLifecycle` with `signal`, `disposed`, `reason`, `track(op)`, `pending()`, `settle(ops, failures)`, `withTimeout(op)`, `close()`.
- **Data flow:** `close()` aborts one `AbortController` with a `TEAM_DISPOSED` reason. `track` adds admitted promises to a set and removes them on settle. `settle` awaits `Promise.allSettled` under a timeout and pushes only *non-cancellation* rejections into a `failures` array.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) `isCancellation` walks the **`cause` chain** with a `Set` guard against cycles, and recognizes both the exact abort reason object and any `TeamError` with code `TEAM_DISPOSED` — so a cancellation wrapped in a cause chain still counts as expected; (b) disposal failures are *collected*, not thrown immediately, and re-thrown as an `AggregateError` by the caller.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `withTimeout` races the operation against a timer and clears the timer in a `finally`; the timeout error carries `TEAM_DISPOSAL_TIMEOUT`.
- **Surprising:** the README notes `disposalTimeoutMs` "is not a whole-service shutdown bound" — each Team child drain gets its own deadline.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/task-graph.ts`
- **Purpose:** complete dependency validation for the task DAG.
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamTaskGraphViolation = 'missing' | 'duplicate' | 'cycle'`; `TeamTaskGraphError`; `assertTaskGraphCandidate(current, candidate)`.
- **Data flow:** builds a `Map` of current tasks plus the candidate, then for each non-deleted task checks each blocker for self-reference (`cycle`), repetition (`duplicate`), and existence/non-deleted (`missing`); then runs a DFS with `visiting`/`visited` sets to detect cycles.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) validation runs against the **whole active graph** after replacing one candidate — a single bad edge anywhere invalidates the write; (b) deleted tasks are skipped, so a deleted blocker is treated as "missing" rather than as a valid blocker; (c) the violation category is a **field on the error** so the command layer can map it to a stable code without string-matching the message.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** the DFS `visit` returns early for missing or deleted tasks, so a dangling edge cannot crash the walk.
- **Surprising:** the mapping to codes in `task-board.ts` sends `duplicate` to `TEAM_INVALID_ARGUMENT` — a duplicate blocker is an argument error, while a cycle is its own code and a missing blocker is `TEAM_TASK_NOT_FOUND`.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/task-view.ts`
- **Purpose:** pure derivation of the task view shared by the board and the client projection.
- **Key abstractions:** `taskReady(state, task)`; `projectTaskView(state, task) → TeamTaskView`; private `scopesOverlap(left, right)`.
- **Data flow:** state + one task → owner name (`lead` for the root, else the member's name), readiness (all blockers `completed`), and **write-scope overlap warnings** against every other `in_progress` task.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) `scopesOverlap` compares **path components** (`left.startsWith(right + '/')`), so `src/a` does not overlap `src/ab` — a naive prefix test would produce false warnings; (b) warnings are a `Set` (deduped) and are purely advisory; (c) the JSDoc notes a committing caller may pass its *pre-append* state, because the candidate task supplies the new value explicitly and "owner names, blocker readiness, and other task scopes do not change when that snapshot is appended".
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `ownerName` is omitted entirely (not `undefined`) under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` — see the `...ownerName === undefined ? {} : { ownerName }` spread idiom.
- **Surprising:** `ready` is `task.status === 'pending' && taskReady(...)` — a task that is already `in_progress` reports `ready: false` even if its blockers completed.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/projection.ts`
- **Purpose:** the strict replay projection over the Lead's Session log, and the browser wire view.
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamState` (members/tasks/messages/delivered/`nextTaskNumber`); `TeamProjectionState` (= state + optional `failure`); `teamProjectionDefinition` (`key: 'agentTeam'`, `stateVersion: 4`); `isTeamEvent`; `teamProjectionView`.
- **Data flow:** every committed Session event is fed to `applyProjectionEvent`, which first checks the `teamId` selector and `version === 2`, then dispatches to `applyCurrentTeamEvent`, which **mutates a new state object** and replaces only the collection it touched ("untouched collections keep their references").
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the projection is a **validator as well as a projector** — a member must begin `provisioning`; `provisioning → active|failed` only; immutable identity fields (`name`, `provider`, `context`) may not change; a task must begin at revision 1 and increment contiguously; a name may not be reused by another member; a message may not be queued twice nor delivered before queueing nor delivered twice. Any violation sets `state.failure` and **stops applying further events** ("`if (state.failure !== undefined) return state`"). (b) the client view is **memoised on collection identity** with a `WeakMap<members, WeakMap<tasks, TeamProjection>>` so a mailbox-only change publishes no frame. (c) `contentBlockSchema` deliberately keeps unknown JSON objects **by reference** — the comment says "loose-object parsing drops their own `__proto__` keys" — and the retired tool-result tag may not enter the merge-extensible fallback.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** a failure is **terminal**: "later events retain the failed state reference and do not republish its view". `parsePersisted` wraps the zod error as the `cause` of a plain `Error` so the original decode detail survives.
- **Surprising:** the projection is *not* a mirror of the durable log — it is a **state machine with invariants**. A corrupt log does not produce a corrupt board; it produces `failure` plus the last valid state.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/task-board.ts`
- **Purpose:** the task DAG commands (create, get, list, compare-and-set update).
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamTaskBoard` with `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`; `TASK_GRAPH_ERROR_CODES`; private `dependencies`, `writeScopes`, `assertTaskGraph`, `withoutOwner`.
- **Data flow:** every command runs inside `journal.transact(root.id, …)`, so the read-check-append is atomic against the Lead log. `update` reads the current task, compares `expectedRevision` (stale → `TEAM_TASK_STALE_REVISION`), authorizes, computes the next snapshot, validates the graph, appends `team/task` with `revision: current.revision + 1`, and returns the projected view.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) **compare-and-set on every mutation** — "an update based on an outdated copy is rejected, so two members cannot silently overwrite each other's work"; (b) `claim` requires `status === 'pending' && taskReady(...)`, and `reassign` by the Lead also requires readiness, but a task with an owner may still be *released*; (c) `delete` is refused while another non-deleted task lists it as a blocker (`TEAM_TASK_HAS_DEPENDENTS`); (d) `reassign` with an empty owner **unassigns and returns the task to `pending`** rather than erroring; (e) deleted tasks remain as tombstones and do not count against `maxTasks`.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `maxTasks` counts **non-deleted** tasks only; id-space exhaustion reports `TEAM_TASK_LIMIT` rather than reusing the last id; `delete` on a task with dependents is refused; `withoutOwner` uses the exactOptionalPropertyTypes-safe destructure idiom.
- **Surprising:** the `claim` path deliberately does *not* call `authorizeOwner()` — a non-lead, non-owner may **claim** an unowned task; ownership authorization only applies to mutations of an already-owned task.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/roster.ts`
- **Purpose:** Team identity, membership resolution, continuable-child provisioning, and roster teardown.
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamMembership` (`{ root, id, role, name }`); `TeamRoster` with `membership`, `tryMembership`, `list`, `spawn`, `recoverFor`, `interrupt`, `liveChildrenByRoot`, `stopTeammates`; exported `resolveActiveMember(root, state, rawName)`.
- **Data flow:** `spawn` → validate name/description/provider → append a `provisioning` member record and flush → `ctx.subagents.startActivation({ delivery: 'parent', childId, provider, … })` → `checkpointInitialPrompt` (flush the child's Session until the initial prompt is durably accepted) → append the terminal `active` member. A failure appends a `failed` member instead.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) **the Lead is implicit** — "Every ordinary runtime root is the implicit Lead of a Team whose `TeamId` equals its `SessionId`; there is no creation event"; (b) `tryMembership` distinguishes three cases: a rostered child (teammate), a plain child of a root (an *independent* root Team — "Ordinary host forks are independent roots"), and a child carrying a subagent descriptor (must **not** receive a nested Team identity); (c) `tryMembership` wraps everything in a `try/catch` and returns `undefined` on a malformed durable stream, with the comment "the non-throwing probe must not veto unrelated Agent lifecycle edges"; (d) names are **reserved by the first provisioning record and never reused** — "even a teammate whose creation failed keeps its name"; (e) `checkpointInitialPrompt` loops on `session/event` / `session/disposed` until the message is accepted, and falls back to reading the *persisted* Session when the child is not in the registry.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** a `TEAM_PROVISIONING_CONFLICT` is raised if the creator reports failure but recovery already settled the member as `active`; if both the creation *and* the durable failure record fail, an `AggregateError` carries both; if the *final* `active` checkpoint fails, the in-memory active edge is kept rather than inventing an impossible `active → failed` transition. `reconcileProvisioning` reads the child's persisted Session and only promotes to `active` when parent, continuable descriptor, provider and an accepted initial user message all match — otherwise `failed` with a reason.
- **Surprising:** `interrupt` uses `{ kind: 'ancestor', agent: caller }` and `keepInbox` semantics — it cancels only the current turn and **does not** release task ownership or delete queued mail.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/index.ts`
- **Purpose:** the service façade (`TeamService extends Service`) over roster, journal, activity, lifecycle and task board.
- **Key abstractions:** `TeamService` with `static inject = ['agents','sessions','sessionPersistence','sessionProjections','subagents']`; `static Config` (a schemastery `z` schema with defaults 16 / 256 / 65,536 / 5,000); the public methods `membership`, `listMembers`, `spawnTeammate`, `sendMessage`, `createTask`, `getTask`, `listTasks`, `updateTask`, `waitForChange`, `interrupt`, `tryMembership`.
- **Data flow:** the constructor wires the five collaborators, subscribes to `agent/created` (schedule recovery) and `agent/status` (notify waiters), registers the projection via `ctx.effect`, and walks `ctx.agents.list()` to recover pre-existing agents. `sendAdmitted` resolves the target, rejects self-messages, frames the content with a `Team message from <name>:` prefix, bounds the **complete sender-framed UTF-8** payload against `maxMessageBytes`, and either `root.steer(input)` (target is the Lead) or `steerHostSubagentPrompt(...)` (target is a teammate).
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) every public method takes the **exact live calling `Agent`** as the authority credential — "Explicit authority"; (b) `sendMessage` composes `AbortSignal.any([request.signal, this.lifecycle.signal])` so a disposed runtime cancels in-flight sends; (c) `scheduleRecovery` uses `queueMicrotask` to run "after publication has unwound", and swallows the failure with a `logger.warn` rather than crashing; (d) `disposeRuntime` closes admission, closes waiters, settles tracked operations, drains roster children, and throws an `AggregateError` if any cleanup failed.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `positiveLimit` rejects non-safe-integer or <1 config values with `TEAM_INVALID_CONFIG`; `sendAdmitted` throws `TEAM_SELF_MESSAGE`; `messageId` for a Lead target is the `UserMessage` id, for a teammate it is the inbox id returned by the host Steer path.
- **Surprising:** a send is "accepted" at the **target inbox**, not processed by the model — the README is explicit that "Success means inbox acceptance, not model processing".

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/client.ts`
- **Purpose:** a client-safe surface for the browser.
- **Key abstractions:** re-exports `TeamMemberPhase`, `TeamMemberProjection`, `TeamMemberView`, `TeamProjection`, `TeamTaskId`, `TeamTaskStatus`, `TeamTaskView` — types only.
- **Data flow:** the Web client imports `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team/client` to get the wire vocabulary without pulling in the Node-side service.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** the split exists so the browser bundle cannot accidentally import the service (which depends on `dsh-session-persistence`, `dsh-subagent`, etc.).
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** n/a — it is a pure type re-export.
- **Surprising:** the *durable* `TeamTaskSnapshot` is deliberately **not** in the client surface; the browser only ever sees the derived view.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/src/index.ts` / `package.json` / `tsconfig.json` / `tsdown.config.ts` / `locale/en.json` / `locale/zh.json`
- `package.json` — public package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team` v`0.2.1-rc.2`, `publishConfig.access: public`, three runtime entry points (`.`, `./client`, `./types`), and the workspace deps it needs (`dsh-brand`, `schemastery`, `zod` as runtime; `dsh-agent`, `dsh-llm`, `dsh-session`, `dsh-session-persistence`, `dsh-session-projection`, `dsh-subagent` as peers). The dev deps list the two subagent providers (`dsh-subagent-fork-in-process`, `dsh-subagent-spawn-in-process`) — the providers are pluggable.
- `tsconfig.json` — `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and explicit project references to every workspace it consumes (brand, llm, session, agent, subagent, session-persistence, session-projection).
- `tsdown.config.ts` — builds `lib/types/index.js` into `lib` as ESM, `target: es2024`, `dts: false` (types are emitted by `tsc`), `clean: false`.
- `locale/en.json` / `locale/zh.json` — the plugin-manager title and description ("Team Collaboration" / "团队协作").

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/README.md`
- **Purpose:** the package contract; the most valuable single document in this shard.
- **Key abstractions:** four stated commitments — "Durable log, derived state", "Process-local ownership", "Explicit authority", "Bounds that fail loud".
- **Data flow:** documents the whole lifecycle: identity → roster → messages → task board → waiting → durability → disposal, plus the Model Experience (token effect and KV-cache effect per feature).
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** the README states its *negative* guarantees as carefully as its positive ones — "Team does not retain unaccepted send intent, retry new messages after restart, or deduplicate explicit resends"; "Deleted tasks remain in history but disappear from the active list"; "File hints produce warnings … they never block anything".
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** the limits table gives defaults for `maxMembers` (16), `maxTasks` (256), `maxMessageBytes` (65,536), `disposalTimeoutMs` (5,000) and says they are "validated at startup".
- **Surprising:** a whole section is spent on **what the team cannot do** — flat immutable roster, no nested teams, no automatic ownership release, no cross-process mailbox, no worktree isolation. And the "Whole-view broadcasts" limitation admits that every roster change ships the full board to every connected browser.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team-profile/*` (the composition bundle)
- `packages/experimental/agent-team-profile/cordis.patch.yml` — the entire runtime content of the profile: it **disables** four base tools (`tool-subagent-control`, `tool-subagent-list-agents`, `tool-subagent`, `tool-subagent-fork`) and **inserts** the Team service (`maxMembers: 8`, `maxTasks: 256`, `maxMessageBytes: 65536`, `disposalTimeoutMs: 5000`), the Team tools (`freshProvider: spawn`, `forkProvider: fork`) and the Team UI. A whole "profile" is therefore a *patch document*, not code.
- `packages/experimental/agent-team-profile/src/index.ts` — an empty module (`export {}`); the comment says the runtime content is the `dsh.bundle.patch` document and "this module exports no runtime API".
- `packages/experimental/agent-team-profile/tests/profile.spec.ts` — pins the *composition contract* by parsing the YAML with `entryListSchema` and asserting the four tools are disabled and the three inserted rows carry the expected names and config. A configuration file is tested as if it were code.
- `packages/experimental/agent-team-profile/README.md` — explains that the bundle "ships with dsh switched off", that "the same bundle switch controls the tools and browser UI", and that the UI plugin "has an inert Host entry; only the Web Client loader mounts its browser entry, so headless needs no Web server". Documents the token/KV-cache effect: "it adds no prompt text of its own" and "Team identity is appended through runtime-context snapshots".
- `packages/experimental/agent-team-profile/package.json` / `locale/*.json` / `tsconfig.json` — manifest with `dsh.bundle.patch: './cordis.patch.yml'`, `publishConfig.access: public`, and the three workspace deps; bilingual plugin-manager title/description; tsconfig referencing the three sibling packages.

#### `packages/experimental/agent-team/tests/*` — the test contract (Tier 2)

| File | What it is / what it pins |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/experimental/agent-team/tests/team.spec.ts` | The largest suite (66 KB, ~40 cases in 4 `describe` blocks). Pins: missing/failed projections are rejected; limits must be positive safe integers; direct-constructor defaults; fresh **and** fork teammates with immutable names and a bounded roster; the child's accepted prompt is flushed **before** the active roster edge commits; live and detached inbox receipts are checkpointed and an unresolved checkpoint aborts; an accepted child is drained when its checkpoint fails; a failed provisioning is recorded durably, **reserves its name** and counts against the limit; non-`Error` provider failures and a reversed provisioning race are contained; only the Lead may create/interrupt; a plain fork becomes a new root Team and inherited Team state is filtered; stale identities and non-Team subagent children are rejected; numeric task-id exhaustion fails loudly; deleted tasks are tombstones that do not count against the limit; CAS + ownership + dependencies + transitions + write-scope warnings; Lead reassign/complete/reopen/delete permissions; peer and Lead messages carry the *actual* sender identity and wake waits; an idle Lead is steered and a cold sibling is resumed with sender attribution; concurrent sends bypass the Team queue; a failed send retains no intent and leaves the service usable; sends are cancellable; task commits are serialized while sends use the independent inbox owner; UTF-8 byte limits are enforced on the complete framed payload; interrupt cancels only the current turn and keeps an accepted follow-up; waits time out, cancel, and release on HMR disposal; disposal drains live activations, closes creation admission, bounds a never-settling drain, shares one settlement deadline, and reports teardown failures. |
| `packages/experimental/agent-team/tests/persistence.spec.ts` | JSONL-backed **crash-restart** tests. Pins: an accepted target inbox is restored from the child's flushed crash prefix with **no Team send intent** (the Lead log contains no `team/message/*` event); a persisted child reconciles to `active` while a missing child reconciles to durable `failed` with an error; a child whose initial prompt is durably *pending* reconciles to `active` **without issuing any model request**; historical queued mail stays readable but is never delivered after restart. |
| `packages/experimental/agent-team/tests/projection-events.spec.ts` | The projection as a **state machine**. Pins: a retired `tool-result` content block is rejected on a V4 checkpoint restore; records for another `teamId` are ignored even when malformed; a member must begin `provisioning` and may only go `provisioning → active|failed`; identity fields are immutable; a name may not be reused; a task begins at revision 1 and increments contiguously; every invalid dependency relation (missing / self / duplicate / cycle / deleted blocker) throws; a numeric id outside the safe-integer range is rejected; a message cannot be queued twice, delivered before queueing, re-targeted, or delivered twice; every malformed payload is rejected with a typed message; merge-extensible content blocks survive; `__proto__`/`constructor` keys are preserved through projection **and** checkpoint round-trip without prototype pollution; a lossy V3 checkpoint is rebuilt from the original log; an unsupported event version sets `failure` and stops applying events; the state is copy-on-write per collection; the client view is reused for mailbox-only changes; publication is per-Session. |
| `packages/experimental/agent-team/tests/built-lib.e2e.ts` | Plain-Node smoke of the **built** artifact: `packages/experimental/agent-team/lib/index.js` must import under plain Node and export a class named `TeamService`. `describe.skipIf` when the artifact is absent, so it never fails a source-only checkout. |
| `packages/experimental/agent-team/tests/test-session-query.ts` | A test-only `SessionQueryEngine` subclass: `observeSession` prefers the live Session and otherwise reads through a short-lived persistence handle; `searchSessions`/`searchEvents` reject because search is out of scope for these tests. |

### Tier 1 — `packages/experimental/tool-agent-team` (the model-facing Team surface)

#### `packages/experimental/tool-agent-team/src/index.ts`
- **Purpose:** register the nine model-facing Team tools **inside each Team member's own Agent scope**.
- **Key abstractions:** `name = 'tool-agent-team'`, `inject = ['agents','agentTeams','tools','systemPrompt']`; `Config` (`interrupt`, `freshProvider`, `forkProvider`); `teamPolicy(interrupt)` — one long fixed policy string; `jsonOutput(schema)` — a helper that pairs a canonical output schema with a compact-JSON renderer; the nine tools: `spawn_teammate`, `send_message`, `list_agents`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, `team_task_create`, `team_task_list`, `team_task_get`, `team_task_update`.
- **Data flow:** `apply(ctx, config)` walks `ctx.agents.list()`, installs into every agent where `ctx.agentTeams.tryMembership(agent)` is defined, and subscribes to `agent/created` / `agent/disposed`. `install(agent, ctx, config)` registers (a) a `team:policy` **system-prompt section** at a named order, (b) a **required** `team:identity` context whose text is a *function* of the current membership, and (c) the tools on `agent.ctx` (not the global `ctx`).
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) **scoped, not global** — every registration lives on the member Agent's own context, so the same tool name shadows the legacy global subagent control *for team members only*; (b) `jsonOutput` exists so "the compiler checks `execute` against the value the model is promised" and no result spends tokens on indentation; (c) `modelMember()` strips the internal `id` and exposes the **name** as the model-facing `target` — the model never sees a Session id; (d) `wait_agent` has a **model-only shortcut**: if no other member is `running`/`provisioning`, it returns `{ timedOut: false, noProgress: { reason: 'no-active-peer', message: … } }` **immediately** instead of burning the timeout; (e) the shortcut's peer read and the waiter registration must be **one synchronous span** — the comment says "awaiting between them can lose the only peer-status edge"; (f) invalid `timeout_ms` is passed to the service so the service's authoritative validation runs, rather than being silently clamped.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** the install is wrapped in try/catch that unwinds **already-registered disposers in reverse order** so a failed install cannot leave a partial scope; the disposer does the same on teardown; `team_task_list` validates `cursor ≥ 0` and `limit ∈ [1,100]`; `team_task_list` returns `nextCursor` only when more rows remain.
- **Surprising:** the **policy text itself is a safety contract**: "Split write work into disjoint scopes… Write-scope overlap is advisory, not a lock"; "If a file operation returns FS_STALE_VERSION, read the current file, rebase… and retry"; "Bash, formatters, code generators, and scripts are not fully protected by the filesystem version guard"; "Task readiness never starts an owner"; "A successful send does not mean the recipient has processed it"; "The Lead must wait for required teammates before giving the final answer." The README calls this out as "**Prompt policy is coordination, not confinement**".

#### `packages/experimental/tool-agent-team/README.md`
- **Purpose:** the package contract for the tool adapter.
- **Key abstractions:** three commitments — "Scoped, not global", "Declared results, compact JSON", "The domain owns authority" ("Tools delegate to `ctx.agentTeams`… the adapter adds no weaker path").
- **Data flow:** documents the nine tools grouped into four capabilities, the two config fields, and the "no Session ID in results" rule.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** the README's "Token effect" / "KV Cache effect" subsections state the *cost* of the feature: "Fixed policy and schema cost on every Team member request", "An unchanged retained snapshot adds no message; changed or removed context causes the loop to append a complete snapshot, including identity."
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** "`send_message` returns `{ "sent": true }` after inbox acceptance, **without exposing the message ID**"; "`wait_agent` returns `noProgress` right away when no other member is running or provisioning".
- **Surprising:** "It replaces legacy subagent controls with the same tool names, so compositions that need both must disable the legacy definitions" — a **name collision** is handled by the *bundle patch*, not by the tool layer.

### Tier 1 — `packages/experimental/tool-session-query` (structured logs the model can query)

#### `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/src/index.ts`
- **Purpose:** five read-only tools that let a model search and read its own prior session history.
- **Key abstractions:** `DEFAULT_MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS = 100`, `DEFAULT_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`; `Config` (`maxSearchResults`, `searchTimeoutMs` bounded by `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`); the five tools `session_search`, `session_event_search`, `session_trace`, `session_event_trace`, `session_event_read`.
- **Data flow:** `apply(ctx, config)` adds one prompt section and registers the five tools, each with a `timeoutMs` and a `presentCall` presenter. The three exact trace/read tools set `isConcurrencySafe: () => true`; the two search tools do not — because "one search consumes generation-bound provider cursors".
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the prompt section is a **fixed, prefix-stable** string so the request prefix stays cacheable; (b) the model is given **no cursor, offset, page size, or model-controlled limit** — the cap is deployment-owned and a capped result tells the model to narrow its query; (c) `resolveConfig` re-validates the config even though the schemastery schema already did, and throws a `TypeError` naming the package.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `searchTimeoutMs` must be a positive integer ≤ `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`; `maxSearchResults` must be a positive safe integer.
- **Surprising:** "The package performs **no byte or character truncation** and does not import a spill backend; deployments that need bounded inline output mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-spill-policy`" — bounded output is a *deployment* concern, not a tool concern.

#### `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/src/service-boundary.ts`
- **Purpose:** one error sanitizer between the trusted query service and the model.
- **Key abstractions:** `SAFE_SESSION_QUERY_FAILURES` — an exhaustive `Record<SessionQueryErrorCode, ModelSafeServiceFailure>` mapping every service code to a **fixed, non-revealing** message; `serviceBoundary.call(ctx, signal, operation, invoke)`; `serviceBoundary.sanitizeError`; `unauthorizedTarget()`; `renderFullError` (walks the `cause` chain, guards against cycles, joins with `\nCaused by: `).
- **Data flow:** every `ctx.sessionQuery.*` call is wrapped in `serviceBoundary.call`, which checks the signal before and after the call, and on failure logs the **full** diagnostic to `ctx.logger.warn` while throwing a **model-safe** error.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the map is `satisfies Record<SessionQueryErrorCode, …>` so a **new service code is a compile error** until it is classified — this is the single most transferable idea in the shard; (b) two codes are deliberately collapsed to the generic `SESSION_QUERY_TOOL_FAILED` (`INVALID_CONFIG`, `SOURCE_CONFLICT`) because their real message would leak internals; (c) the *local* `SESSION_QUERY_TOOL_UNAUTHORIZED` is kept precise — it is the tool's own message, not the service's; (d) `fullError` is wrapped in its own try/catch and degrades to `'[unprintable session query failure]'`.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** if the logger itself throws, `sanitizeError` returns the generic failure; the whole `try` block is guarded so a misbehaving logger can never break the model call.
- **Surprising:** the *only* thing the model is told about a failure is a code + a fixed English sentence; the real diagnostic lives in the log. The code list even includes `SESSION_QUERY_STALE_CURSOR` → "session history changed while paging; retry the complete search call" — i.e. the model is told to **retry the whole call**, not to resume.

#### `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/src/workspace-access.ts`
- **Purpose:** derive the caller's authority and decide what the model may read.
- **Key abstractions:** `callerOf(exec, ctx)` — the caller identity comes from `exec.agent`, never from the model's arguments; `headerAuthorized` — authority is **exact-string `cwd` equality**; `authorizeTarget`, `authorizeSessionIds`; `readTitles`/`readTitle`; `authorizeDescendants` + `visitDescendants` (an **explicit-stack** generator, not recursion); `titleText`.
- **Data flow:** every operation calls `callerOf` → `targetId` → `authorizeTarget` → service call → `assertObservedTargetAuthorized` (re-checks the header observed *with the result*, not just the one requested).
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) **"Authority derived from the caller, never the model"** — the model cannot name a workspace; (b) a caller with **no `cwd`** may inspect only itself; (c) missing and cross-workspace parent guesses are made **indistinguishable** ("makes hidden and nonexistent parent guesses indistinguishable without calling search"); (d) unauthorized ancestors/descendants are replaced by **markers containing no hidden session id** (`[outside workspace boundary]`, `[outside workspace subtree]`); (e) the descendant walk is an explicit stack so a deep lineage cannot blow the JS call stack — the test name is "renders a deeply nested lineage **without recursive consumer traversal**".
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `readTitles` handles a per-item `rejected` observation by producing an `unavailableTitle` with the *code* but not the diagnostic, and re-throws an authorization failure; `assertObservedTargetAuthorized` rejects a target that "moved after pre-authorization".
- **Surprising:** the exact `cwd` string comparison is deliberately conservative — the README flags "symlink-equivalent paths do not share authority" as an **undecided** future change.

#### `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/src/input.ts`
- **Purpose:** model-facing schemas and the normalization that turns model arguments into service filters.
- **Key abstractions:** `sessionSearchParameters`, `eventSearchParameters`, `targetSessionParameter`; `buildSessionFilters`, `buildEventFilters`, `materializeParentSessionIds`, `normalizeQuery`, `sequenceRange`.
- **Data flow:** the model's snake_case args become `SessionResultFilter[]` / `SessionEventMetadataFilter[]` discriminated unions (`{ kind: 'id' | 'cwd' | 'parent' | 'created-at' | 'availability' | 'seq' | 'time' | 'type' | 'surface', values }`).
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the **exact sub-millisecond timestamp** machinery — `parseIsoTimestamp` keeps a `remainder` of decimal digits below one millisecond, `compareTimestamps` compares remainders digit by digit, and `timestampLowerBound`/`timestampUpperBound` nudge the epoch-ms bound to the **adjacent representable double** (`nextUpFinite`/`nextDownFinite` via `DataView` bit twiddling) so an inclusive bound never **collapses the interval**; (b) `normalizeQuery` rejects whitespace-only and NUL; (c) `assertNonEmptyArray` — an *empty* array is rejected rather than treated as "no filter", because an empty filter list would silently widen the search; (d) `daysInMonth` implements the full Gregorian leap rule, so `2023-02-29` is rejected.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `from > to` is rejected as `SESSION_QUERY_INVALID_FILTER`; `sequenceRange` bounds must be non-negative safe integers; a normalized timestamp that the platform parser cannot turn into a finite value is rejected.
- **Surprising:** the timestamp code exists because SQLite comparisons on floating epoch-ms bounds are **inclusive/exclusive-ambiguous** at sub-millisecond resolution. This is a subtle, real correctness trap.

#### `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/src/operations.ts`
- **Purpose:** the five operation workflows.
- **Key abstractions:** `executeSessionSearch`, `executeEventSearch`, `executeSessionTrace`, `executeEventTrace`, `executeEventRead`; `collectPages(maxResults, signal, request, accept)` — the internal pager.
- **Data flow:** `collectPages` loops on the provider cursor, filters each item through `accept`, stops at the cap with `capped: true`, and **detects a repeated cursor** (`seen` set) → `SESSION_QUERY_INVALID_CURSOR` instead of looping forever.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) **the current session's own search is bounded by the current step**: `range.to = min(range.to, lastStepStartSeq - 1)` — "the current session excludes the step performing this call", so a tool cannot read the turn that is still running; (b) a caller with no `cwd` gets `SESSION_QUERY_TOOL_UNAUTHORIZED` for cross-session search; (c) parent ids are **pre-authorized** and only authorized parents (plus the `null` root marker) are sent as the `parent` filter — an unauthorized parent never reaches the provider; (d) `collectPages` **drains hidden internal pages** to find authorized hits (the cap applies to *authorized* results, not raw pages).
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** a degenerate range (`from > to`) returns an empty result rather than calling the provider; a repeated provider cursor throws; cancellation is checked before and after every page.
- **Surprising:** "Search results are cursor-free" — the *provider* cursor is an internal implementation detail that never reaches the model, and the model is never given a way to ask for "page 2".

#### `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/src/presentation.ts`
- **Purpose:** render the results as plain text and provide the tool-call cards.
- **Key abstractions:** `formatSessionSearch`, `formatEmptySessionSearch`, `formatEventSearch`, `formatSessionTrace`, `formatEventTrace`, `formatEventRead`; `presentSessionSearchCall` / `presentEventSearchCall` / `presentSessionTraceCall` / `presentEventTargetCall` (all `card: 'generic'`).
- **Data flow:** service objects → fixed-format text blocks; the tool-call card shows only the query or the target id + seq.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the **result-cap message is a sentence to the model**, not an error: "Result cap reached. Narrow the query or add filters to find additional matches."; (b) an unauthorized parent is rendered as `[outside workspace]` — never a hidden id; (c) `formatEventRead` emits the target event as **fenced JSON** (`JSON.stringify(window.target, null, 2)`) — unabridged, not summarized; (d) neighbouring events get a **summary line plus optional semantic text**, and "(no semantic text)" when there is none; (e) `presentEventTargetCall` is a **factory** (`(action, args) => …`) so "Trace event" and "Read event" share one presenter.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** availability is rendered `live`, `persisted`, `live, persisted` or `unavailable`; empty relationship lists render as `none`.
- **Surprising:** the presentation layer is the only place that knows how to *say* things to the model — and it deliberately says "Narrow the query" rather than exposing pagination.

#### `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/README.md` and config
- **README.md** — the package contract: five read-only tools, **cursor-free** results, **workspace-scoped** authority, `maxSearchResults` 100 / `searchTimeoutMs` 30 000, and the four design commitments. It also states the failure policy: "caller cancellation is preserved exactly, corpus and provider diagnostics go to the internal log, and unsafe or unprintable failures fall back to the fixed `SESSION_QUERY_TOOL_FAILED` code and message."
- `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/package.json` — the manifest declares **`dsh-session-query` as a peer** and lists `dsh-session-query-sqlite` only as a dev dependency: the backend is a deployment choice, the tool is backend-agnostic.
- `packages/experimental/tool-session-query/tsconfig.json` — project references for every workspace consumed.

### Tier 1 — `packages/experimental/tool-ralph` (bounded fresh-agent iteration)

#### `packages/experimental/tool-ralph/src/index.ts`
- **Purpose:** one `ralph` tool that runs a **fixed** foreground loop of fresh child agents toward one immutable objective.
- **Key abstractions:** `Config` (`subagentProvider`, `maxRounds` 256, `maxHandoffChars` 16 384, `maxResultChars` 16 384); `RalphRoundStatus = 'continue' | 'complete' | 'blocked'`; `RalphRoundReport` (`status`, `summary`, `evidence[]`, `nextSteps[]`, `blocker`); `RalphRunStatus = 'complete' | 'blocked' | 'budget-limited'`; `RALPH_SCRIPT` — a **deployment-owned fixed script**; `readReport` / `readRunResult` — defensive decoders; `boundResult` / `TRUNCATION_NOTICE`.
- **Data flow:** the model submits `{ objective, maxRounds? }`; the tool starts a `ctx.workflowEngine.start({ script: RALPH_SCRIPT, args: {objective, maxRounds, maxHandoffChars}, subagentProvider, maxTotalAgents: maxRounds, parent, signal })`; the script loops `for round = 1..maxRounds`, each round calling `agent(prompt, { schema: reportSchema })` — a **fresh** child that receives only the objective, the round number, the workspace-as-memory instruction, and the previous report; the run ends `complete`, `blocked`, or `budget-limited`; the tool awaits `run.result`, then `run.dispose()` in a `finally`.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) **the model supplies data only** — "it cannot alter the loop, provider route, schema, or handoff validation"; (b) `requireFreshProvider` refuses a provider that lacks `capabilities.outputSchema` or reports `inheritsParentContext: true` — "Ralph requires a fresh provider" — and it fails **before any round starts**; (c) the round cap is carried as `maxTotalAgents` so the engine's own child backstop agrees with the loop; (d) the report is validated **twice** — once inside the fixed script and again at the consumer boundary (`readReport`) — because a provider is a trust boundary; (e) `readReport` checks `Object.keys(value).sort().join(',') === 'blocker,evidence,nextSteps,status,summary'` — an **exact key set**, so an extra key is a malformed report; (f) a `budget-limited` result is only accepted when `roundsStarted === maxRounds` — "Ralph workflow returned budget-limited before the round limit" is an error; (g) the result text says "Ralph **worker reported** completion" — the tool never presents self-report as certification.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `stopReasonError` maps a non-`completed` workflow stop to an error (cancelled / error / unknown); an ordinary child failure is a **tool error** naming the failed round and retaining the last successful handoff; `boundResult` truncates with a visible `… [truncated]` marker and handles a cap shorter than the marker; `exec.signal` is bridged to `run.cancel('parent step aborted')` *and* passed into the engine, and the abort listener is removed in `finally`; `maxRounds` requested by the model is clamped by the **deployment ceiling** (an over-ceiling request is an error, not a silent clamp).
- **Surprising:** the prompt tells each fresh child "**Do not call the ralph tool: this round already is its worker**" and "Treat the previous report only as a bounded handoff; **confirm it against the workspace**" — the previous round's claim is treated as a hint, never as truth. And the README is honest: "**No enforced recursive-Ralph denial** — structural denial is not implemented; prompt guidance does not enforce a recursion ban."

#### `packages/experimental/tool-ralph/README.md` and tests
- **README.md** — states the completion semantics plainly: "**Completion is worker self-declaration** — there is no independent evaluator or verifier deciding whether the objective is complete; evaluator policy and evaluator-driven continuation are deferred." Also: "The workspace is the only cross-round long-term memory", "**Foreground only** — there is no job id, background collection, process-resume checkpoint, scheduler, or wall-clock start policy", "Only round count bounds aggregate effort — token, price, and elapsed-time budgets are deferred", and "Ordinary child failure is terminal for the run — the fixed script reports the failed round and last successful handoff but does not retry."
- `packages/experimental/tool-ralph/tests/tool-ralph.spec.ts` — pins: the fixed workflow starts through the configured fresh provider; blocked and budget-limited are **bounded successful** results; the parent result is bounded and labelled worker-reported; a result limit shorter than the truncation marker; an ordinary child failure reports the round and the last durable handoff; workflow error/cancellation reasons map to tool errors and the run is always disposed; mid-flight cancellation and an already-aborted signal; invalid authority, empty objective, bad round caps and schema-invalid calls are rejected **before start**; missing, unstructured and parent-context-inheriting provider routes are rejected; invalid direct-apply config is rejected before touching injected services; malformed terminal values become errors; a synchronous engine start failure does not invent a run; scoped guidance and pure replay-safe generic presentation; the namespace-plugin export shape.
- `packages/experimental/tool-ralph/tests/integration.spec.ts` — over the **real** spawn provider and a sandboxed PTC stack: distinct empty-seed children, shared cwd, and only the prior bounded handoff cross rounds; a failed round reports the last good handoff; a table-driven case; and cancellation drives the sandboxed process and fresh child to quiescence.

### Tier 1 — `packages/experimental/auto-review` (an LLM as the approval gate)

#### `packages/experimental/auto-review/src/index.ts`
- **Purpose:** replace human approval with an LLM reviewer for every tool call, under the current-session-only **Auto** permission preset.
- **Key abstractions:** `REVIEW_POLICY` — one long fixed policy string (the heart of the package); `AutoReviewDecision` (a closed union: low/allow, medium/allow, medium|high/deny with an optional reason); `ReviewSourceRole = 'human-instruction' | 'direct-parent-instruction' | 'constraint' | 'checkpoint' | 'fact'`; `PendingAction` (`mode: 'native' | 'ptc-inner'`); `ReviewSnapshot` (provider, model, cwd, projectInstructions, history, action); `snapshotAutoReview`; `parseDecision`; `readDecision`; `denied` / `askUser` / `failed`; `AUTO_REVIEW_DENIED_ERROR_NAME` / `AUTO_REVIEW_DENIED_CODE`.
- **Data flow:** the plugin hooks `ctx.on('tools/pre-execute', …, { prepend: true })`. It skips non-Auto sessions, skips the outer `run_code` transport, and otherwise: `workingDirectory.ensure` → `snapshotAutoReview` (freeze the session's *whole* action history) → `ctx.llm.stream` with `temperature: 0`, the fixed policy as `system`, and a four-section user text (`ENVIRONMENT`, `PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS`, `FILTERED_HISTORY`, `PENDING_ACTION`) → `readDecision` → `parseDecision` → a `PreToolDecision` of `deny` / `ask` / `allow`.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) **the review prompt never enters a Session log** ("This review prompt is sent only through `ctx.llm.stream` and never enters a Session log") — the reviewer's own reasoning does not pollute the agent's context; (b) the decision protocol is a **closed shape**: "An allow object has exactly two members, risk and decision, and **never** has reason"; "Never return low with deny, high with allow, or a reason with allow"; `parseDecision` enforces this with a hand-written `topLevelMemberCount` that strips strings and counts `:` at depth 1, so a **repeated JSON member** is detected (`JSON.parse` would silently keep the last one); (c) the **risk taxonomy is by effect, not by tool name** — "First classify the pending action by its actual effects, never by the tool name, message tone, or claimed intention"; (d) **history is role-labelled** — every retained item is tagged as human-instruction / direct-parent-instruction / constraint / checkpoint / fact, and the policy says "No instruction can downgrade a risk class or authorize a high-risk action" and "direct-parent instructions never override human restrictions"; (e) the snapshot **reconstructs the action history from the Session event log** and cross-checks the visible surface against the log, failing closed on any disagreement ("the pending native call disagrees with its logged action", "visible native call logs do not form a started prefix"); (f) the decision is only a **gate**: if the reviewer allows but the downstream policy also allows, the call runs; if the reviewer allows but downstream says `ask`, the user is asked; if the reviewer denies and the approval policy is `never`, the denial is final; (g) the denial is a **typed, persisted** error (`AutoReviewDeniedError` / `AUTO_REVIEW_DENIED`) and the *audited* reason is English while the *displayed* reason is localized (`displayReason: { en, zh }`).
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** a reviewer that emits data after its terminal finish, ends with a non-`stop` reason, emits no terminal finish, emits anything other than zero-or-more reasoning blocks plus exactly one text block, or returns a non-conforming JSON shape is an **error**, not a denial — and a reviewer *failure* is reported as its own error (`failed`), distinct from a denial; `isAborted` is re-read after every await; on disposal the plugin resets every Auto session to `danger-full-access`, aborts the lifecycle, and awaits all in-flight reviews with `Promise.allSettled`.
- **Surprising:** the whole design is "**fail closed**": "Fail closed when actual effects are ambiguous or broader than established scope"; "Deny a medium action if authorization of its action, target, scope, effect, count or duration is missing, conflicting, ambiguous…". And the risk classes are *effect-based*: "a production read is medium even though it is read-only, and sensitive exfiltration is high **even with explicit authorization**."

#### `packages/experimental/auto-review/README.md` (contract)
- Decides: the reviewer is "the final authorization reviewer for exactly one pending tool call"; "Your decision replaces human approval for this call"; the `ask` policy asks the user, `never` is final; every native call and every started PTC inner call is reviewed once, while "the outer `run_code` transport is deliberately excluded".

### Tier 1 — `packages/experimental/hook-protocol` + the two bridges

#### `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/src/types.ts`
- **Purpose:** the dialect-neutral hook vocabulary and the two durable log events.
- **Key abstractions:** `HookDialect = 'claude-code' | 'codex'`; `CommandHook` (`command`, `timeoutSec`); `MatcherGroup` (`matcher?`, `hooks`); `MatcherMode`; `HookOutput` (every field optional); the `hook/invoked` and `hook/result` `SessionEventMap` entries.
- **Data flow:** a bridge produces a `HookOutput`; the protocol turns it into a paired durable event; a host projects the pair.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the events are **log-only** — "like `compaction/*`; NOT a `SurfaceEventType`, carries no `surfaceOp`" — so a hook never enters the conversation surface; (b) `hook/result` pairs to `hook/invoked` by a **`handlerId`**, not by position; (c) `HookOutput` folds the two *distinct* upstream channels (legacy top-level `decision` = approve/block, and `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` = allow/deny/ask) into one enum, with the comment that `'allow'`/`'deny'`/`'ask'` "arise ONLY from a `permissionDecision`, never from a top-level `decision`"; (d) `updatedInput` is **parsed but not honored** — the field exists so a bridge can log-and-warn rather than silently ignoring a request.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** every field of `HookOutput` is optional because "a hook may exercise any subset"; the bridge decides which fields are meaningful for its hook point — "faithful-but-degraded — e.g. Codex ignores `allow`/`ask`".
- **Surprising:** the events "must remain **turn-enclosed**"; `SessionStart` runs before turn 1, so it "gets no `hook/*` record — its injected context is delivered instead".

#### `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/src/codec.ts`
- **Purpose:** decode a hook process outcome into a neutral `HookOutput`.
- **Key abstractions:** `BLOCKING_EXIT_CODE = 2`; `topLevelDecisionOf` (approve/block only); `permissionDecisionOf` (allow/deny/ask only); `parseHookOutput(exitCode, stdout, stderr, expectedEventName?)`; `applyStructured`.
- **Data flow:** exit code first (2 ⇒ block, stderr becomes the reason), then structured stdout **only on exit 0**.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the function is **total** — "malformed JSON remains plain stdout"; (b) JSON is attempted **only when stdout starts with `{`**, matching the reference engines, so plain text is not an error; (c) the `hookEventName` **discriminator guard**: a `hookSpecificOutput` block whose `hookEventName` names a different event (or omits it) has its **event-scoped fields discarded** while the top-level fields and the claimed discriminator survive; (d) `permissionDecision` **overrides** the legacy top-level `decision`; (e) an out-of-band `{"decision":"deny"}` is invalid and **ignored**, so it can never become a real blocking decision.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** structured stdout is ignored on an exit-2 run ("stderr is authoritative"); an unknown decision string is ignored, not coerced; a JSON array stdout parses but yields no fields.
- **Surprising:** the guard is *opt-out* — "applies the block when `expectedEventName` is omitted" — so a caller that forgets to pass the firing event gets the looser behaviour.

#### `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/src/matcher.ts`
- **Purpose:** validate and apply a matcher pattern for both dialects.
- **Key abstractions:** `CLAUDE_LITERAL = /^[A-Za-z0-9_|]+$/`; `matcherDiagnostic(matcher, mode)`; `matchesMatcher(matcher, query, mode)`; `selectHookGroups(groups, query, mode)`.
- **Data flow:** a config pattern + the event's matcher subject (tool name, session source, …) → a boolean; the groups with command hooks that match, in config order.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) **one axis of difference collapsed into a parameter** — "Claude treats alphanumeric/underscore/pipe patterns as literal alternatives and other patterns as regex; Codex treats every non-empty pattern as an unanchored regex"; (b) absent / empty / `'*'` are the three match-all sentinels; (c) an invalid regex is a **non-match at runtime** but a **diagnostic at parse time** — the config parser rejects the whole config before listeners register.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `compileRegex` catches the `RegExp` construction error and returns `undefined`; `matchesMatcher` returns `false` rather than throwing.
- **Surprising:** the same pattern means different things in the two dialects — `Bash` is an exact match in Claude Code and a **substring** match in Codex.

#### `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/src/merge.ts`
- **Purpose:** fold every matched hook's outcome into one most-restrictive result.
- **Key abstractions:** `MergedDecision = 'allow' | 'ask' | 'deny' | 'none'`; `MergedHookOutcome`; `rank(decision)`; `decisionForRank(maxRank)`; `mergeHookOutputs(outputs)`.
- **Data flow:** a list of `HookOutput`s in hook order → one `MergedHookOutcome`.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the precedence is `deny > ask > allow` (rank 3/2/1); (b) **reasons are collected per rank** and only the **winning rank's** reasons are joined — "when deny wins over ask, the ask reasons are dropped"; (c) the first `continue:false` **stop is sticky** and captures that hook's `stopReason`; (d) `additionalContext` and `systemMessage` accumulate in hook order without joining ("the bridge decides"); (e) an empty list yields `decision: 'none'` — "the caller treats that as 'no hook had anything to say'".
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `block`/`deny` both fold to `deny`; `approve`/`allow` both fold to `allow`; a `continue:false` with no `stopReason` still stops, with an undefined reason.
- **Surprising:** the merged `stop` has **no run-level effect** — the README's "Future: run-level halt" section says the interception points "lack a hard-halt primitive" and the request is "recorded but has no run-level effect".

#### `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/src/runner.ts`
- **Purpose:** run a command hook through the platform's shell executor and decode the outcome.
- **Key abstractions:** `DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000`; `RunHookOptions`; `RunHookResult`; `runHook(bash, hook, options, now)`.
- **Data flow:** serialize the payload to stdin (with an optional trailing newline), run through `ctx.shell`, map the exit code, decode, and report the wall-clock duration.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the hook runs through the **existing shell executor** rather than a bespoke spawn — "the executor already provides the scrubbed-but-overridable environment, process-group cancellation, and timeout the protocol needs"; (b) the per-hook timeout is in **seconds on the wire** and converted to ms; (c) a **signal death** (`exitCode === null`) maps to `undefined` — "a non-blocking error — no clean exit code to act on"; (d) an executor rejection becomes an outcome with **no exit code** and the message on stderr — "The turn proceeds"; the function **never throws**.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** the timeout override is `hook.timeoutSec * 1000`; the default is the deployment's `defaultTimeoutMs`; the abort signal is threaded through.
- **Surprising:** "**Never throw into the loop**" is a stated design commitment — every failure mode degrades to a contained outcome.

#### `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/src/events.ts` and `src/detached.ts`
- **events.ts** — `appendHookInvoked` / `appendHookResult` write the durable pair; `summarizeStderr(stderr, maxChars)` trims and caps at 500 chars with an ellipsis; `DEFAULT_STDERR_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS = 500` lives **in the library that declares the event**, "so the bridges cannot drift apart on the shared event's default cap"; the recorded `decision` is `output.decision ?? (output.continue === false ? 'stop' : 'pass')`; an absent exit code stays omitted.
- **detached.ts** — `createDetachedRuns()` returns a tracker with a `signal` and `track(run)`; `drain()` **aborts** the signal (killing a still-running hook process rather than awaiting its 10-minute timeout) and then loops `while (inflight.size > 0) await Promise.allSettled(...)` so a chain tracked *during* a drain wave is still awaited; a rejected chain is absorbed by the bookkeeping (but "rejection handling is still the caller's job: an untracked `.catch` is what turns a failure into a logged warning instead of silence").
- **Non-obvious design decisions (detached):** `track` is documented to require the **FULL chain** — "the hook run and its continuation/error handler — so `drain` waits for the side effects (an inject, a warn), not just the process exit".
- **Surprising:** a run tracked *after* `drain` resolves is awaited by nobody — "by then the bridge's listeners are disposed, so nothing can start one".

#### `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/README.md`
- Decides: the library is what a hook *can do*; the pipeline is "a chain of single-purpose steps, one function each: validate the matcher pattern, run the command through the `dsh-shell` executor, decode the outcome, merge … and record the durable `hook/*` event pair"; the four design commitments (one axis of difference → `mode`; the executor owns process control; never throw into the loop; log-only, turn-enclosed events).
- States the user-visible contract: "Fail without stopping the run — any exit code other than 2 is a non-blocking failure: the action proceeds and the failure is logged, and a hook that cannot be started at all is treated the same way"; "If the hook config cannot be read or parsed, the bridge logs a warning and no hooks run; **the agent still starts**."

#### `packages/experimental/hooks-claude-code/src/config.ts` and `src/index.ts`
- **config.ts** — `CLAUDE_EVENTS` (7 events), `parseClaudeCodeConfig(raw, vars)`, `substituteCommand`; a malformed entry is **ignored rather than failing boot**; non-command hooks are returned in `skipped` so the bridge can warn; matchers on `UserPromptSubmit`/`Stop` are **discarded** ("those events have no matcher subject"); an invalid regex throws a `SyntaxError` so the whole config is rejected before listeners register; `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` are substituted at parse time and "a token whose variable is unset stays verbatim".
- **index.ts** — `Config` (`configPath` required, `pluginRoot`, `projectDir`, `defaultTimeoutMs`, `stderrSummaryMaxChars`); `runPoint(point, matchQuery, payload, opts)`; the per-event stdin payload builders (`sessionStartPayload`, `promptPayload`, `preToolPayload`, `postToolPayload`, `stopPayload`, `subagentPayload`); the extension-point wiring: `agent/created` → SessionStart (detached, injects context), `agent/pre-step` → UserPromptSubmit → `PreStepDecision`, `tools/pre-execute` → PreToolUse → `PreToolDecision` (`deny`/`ask`), `tools/post-execute` → PostToolUse → `PostToolDecision` (`block` + feedback), `agent/turn-stopping` → Stop (a blocking Stop hook **steers** to force continuation), `subagent/start` / `subagent/end`.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) a blocking **Stop** hook **steers the agent** rather than stopping it — "A blocking Stop hook steers at the stopping boundary, which makes the machine observe pending input and run another step"; (b) the bridge **delegates** (`await next()`) before attaching its own context, so "a later denial, cancellation, or `ask` takes precedence"; (c) `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` defaults **per run** to the agent's current directory, "the same dir the hook runs in"; (d) `updatedInput` and `systemMessage` are logged-and-warned, not honored; (e) the payload's `transcript_path` is **always empty** — "The persistence seam exposes no artifact path; the field stays empty (a durable consumer gap recorded in this package's README)".
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** a config read/parse failure logs a warning and **registers nothing** but the agent still starts; the subagent child is retained in a `Map<SubagentRunId, Agent>` "through its paired end so stop hooks keep the session workspace after the handle unregisters the agent"; `assertPositiveInteger('stderrSummaryMaxChars', …)` runs **before** the config parse "so a bad value cannot be hidden by its early return".
- **Surprising:** `SUBAGENT_TYPE = 'general-purpose'` — the harness subagent seam carries no per-kind label, so the bridge uses Claude Code's own default, meaning "a hooks.json with a default/`*`/empty `agent_type` matcher fires; a config matching a specific kind (e.g. `code-reviewer`) does not". And there is a `TODO(stop-loop-guard)`: "cap consecutive forced continuations; hooks must self-limit meanwhile".

#### `packages/experimental/hooks-codex/src/config.ts` and `src/index.ts`
- **config.ts** — `CODEX_EVENTS` (5 events); `parseCodexConfig` records an `async: true` command hook as **skipped** ("only synchronous command hooks run"); accepts `timeout` or the `timeoutSec` alias; performs **no command substitution**; the matcher-group parsing is marked `/* jscpd:ignore-start */` with the comment "Matcher-group parsing remains dialect-local because the supported hook shapes and skip reasons differ from Claude Code's".
- **index.ts** — the same five extension points with Codex's dialect: **snake_case** payloads, `model` on every event, `turn_id` on turn-scoped events, `permission_mode: 'default'`, `transcript_path: null`, **no trailing newline** on stdin, **no hook environment**, **no pre-tool `ask`** ("Codex blocks only"), and **clean plain stdout becomes `additionalContext`** at SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit ("nonzero output and raw JSON never leak as prose").
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) `tool_name` is the **real** tool name — "a hardcoded constant would disagree with what the matcher tests and make a config's tool matcher never fire"; (b) `tool_input` keeps Codex's `{ command }` shape, derived from the call's `command` argument; (c) the `stop_hook_active` flag is **always false**, so "an unconditionally blocking hook force-continues every step until it self-limits" (a `TODO(stop-loop-guard)`); (d) a blocking Stop hook with **no reason** still forces continuation — "fall back to a generic steering line rather than letting the turn stop".
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** the config is read **once at load**; a read/parse failure logs a warning and registers nothing; the SessionStart chain is tracked in `detached` so disposal aborts a still-running hook process.
- **Surprising:** the two bridges are near-duplicates by design — the source comments explain why: "Each dialect bridge keeps its complete dependency list visible at the entry point; a cross-package facade for imports alone would add indirection."

#### `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/tests/*` (Tier 2)
| File | What it pins |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/tests/codec.spec.ts` | Exit-code semantics (0 neutral, 2 blocking with stderr as reason, other non-zero non-blocking, undefined exit no decision); structured stdout only on exit 0; a top-level `allow`/`deny`/`ask` is **invalid and ignored**; `permissionDecision` overrides the legacy decision; the `hookEventName` guard discards a mismatched or missing discriminator but **not** the event-agnostic top-level fields; malformed JSON is lenient; plain text stdout is left for the bridge; structured stdout is ignored on an exit-2 run. |
| `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/tests/matcher.spec.ts` | Match-all sentinels; Claude literal exact-match (not substring) vs pipe alternation; Codex unanchored regex; invalid regex is a non-match; `matcherDiagnostic` returns a stable message; `selectHookGroups` selects nonempty matching groups in config order and keeps the two dialects distinct. |
| `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/tests/merge.spec.ts` | `deny > ask > allow` regardless of order; only the winning rank's reasons survive; stop is sticky on the first `continue:false`; `additionalContext`/`systemMessages` accumulate in hook order, skipping empties. |
| `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/tests/runner.spec.ts` | The payload is serialized to stdin with/without a trailing newline; env and cwd are threaded; `timeoutSec` overrides the default; the signal passes through; a signal death decodes as an undefined exit; an executor rejection becomes a non-blocking error and never throws; a non-Error rejection is stringified onto stderr; `expectedEventName` is threaded. |
| `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/tests/events.spec.ts` | `hook/invoked` records the matcher when present and omits an absent/undefined one; `hook/result` derives `decision`/`exitCode`/`stderrSummary`; the decision falls back to `stop` on `continue:false` else `pass`; stderr is trimmed and truncated to 500 chars with an ellipsis, and a 500-char stderr is kept verbatim ("the cap is exclusive"); an invoked/result pair correlates by `handlerId`. |
| `packages/experimental/hook-protocol/tests/detached.spec.ts` | `drain` fires the signal; an empty registry resolves immediately; a tracked run is awaited; a run tracked **while** a prior wave was settling is also awaited; a rejected run is absorbed by the bookkeeping. |

### Tier 1 — `packages/experimental/translator` (durable, audited, provider-independent records)

#### `packages/experimental/translator/src/storage.ts`
- **Purpose:** durable, provider-independent translations written through the Session's **existing writer**.
- **Key abstractions:** `TranslationLog` (`request(data) → SessionSeq`, `result(requestSeq, text)`); `TranslationStorage.run(id, identity, signal, operation)`; `identityKey(identity)`; `lookup(...)`; `read(...)`.
- **Data flow:** `run` first **looks up** a saved result by `JSON.stringify([sessionId, identityKey])`; on a miss it appends a `plugin:translator/request` record, **flushes the Session**, and then **reads the record back** to confirm durability ("confirms durability through storage"); on success it appends `plugin:translator/result` with the request's `SessionSeq`; a later `lookup` replays the log, rebuilds a request→result index, and matches by identity.
- **Non-obvious design decisions:** (a) the **request record is written before dispatch** and the **result record before the caller sees the text** — a crash between them leaves a durable request with no result, which is exactly the "settlement" shape; (b) the writer **never opens a write handle and never activates a Session** — "The translator never opens a write handle or activates a Session"; (c) identical concurrent translations **share one attempt**: "Identical concurrent translations wait for the first attempt and its accepted writes, even if its consumer has already canceled or timed out, then reuse its durable result"; (d) the identity includes a **`recipe`** — the protocol revision plus a SHA-256 fingerprint of the effective endpoint, so a changed endpoint invalidates the cache without storing the raw URL; (e) a **malformed** stored record rejects **all** lookups for that Session ("the service does not skip or repair those records") rather than silently skipping it.
- **Edge cases & failure handling:** `current()` re-checks the signal and the persistence identity after **every** await; `live()` re-checks that the Session is still the same object; a cache miss with no **active** Session rejects with `TRANSLATION_SESSION_INACTIVE` *before* the provider is called; `failure()` maps `SessionPersistenceNotFoundError` → `TRANSLATION_SESSION_REQUIRED` and anything else → `TRANSLATION_STORAGE_ERROR`; disposal awaits all pending writes.
- **Surprising:** the durable *request* record carries the **exact model request** (`config`, `system`, `messages`) for paid routes — "Paid request metadata stores `modelRequest: { config, system, messages }` exactly as prepared before dispatch; **credentials are excluded**". That is a real audit trail.

#### `packages/experimental/translator/src/types.ts` and `src/error.ts`
